Corrupting `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_dadd` during target calculation changes one or more bits of the value presented to the software-PC input. The implementation carries the effect through `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_dadd -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. At the following PC write, execution is redirected to an unintended aligned or misaligned address.

Instruction words, extension words, and interrupt vectors return through the memory-backbone path before they influence decode or `pc_nxt`. `openMSP430.fe_mab` carries an address, returned word, or memory-path qualifier on that route; the route is implemented by the corresponding combinational or registered assignment. A fault on `openMSP430.fe_mab` during a fetch or vector read can substitute a wrong instruction/extension or address the wrong program-memory location. The implementation carries the effect through `openMSP430.fe_mab -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`. The resulting decode or vector value drives an incorrect PC transition and breaks control-flow integrity.
